bad.en: (meant: a passer-by and I looked for my dropped wallet together for five minutes)
bad.why: It implies a lasting partnership toward a goal, not a few minutes' help from a stranger. Say issho ni sagashita.

cards.mean: asking oneself questions and answering them
cards.lit: asking oneself, answering oneself

use.how: 〜かと自問自答する / 自問自答を繰り返す: said of reflection or inner debate, such as wondering whether a choice was right.

cards.cue: Lying awake after quitting your job, you keep asking yourself whether it was right, answering, then asking again.

ctx.s: 本当[ほんとう]にこれでいいのか、{自問自答[じもんじとう]}した。
ctx.en: I asked myself whether this was really all right.

ctx.s: 「何[なに]をぶつぶつ言[い]ってるの？」「ちょっと{自問自答[じもんじとう]}してただけ。」
ctx.en: "What are you muttering about?" "Oh, just arguing with myself."

ctx.en: Before bed, I make a habit of asking myself how I did today.

ctx.s: 会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]めるべきか、何日[なんにち]も{自問自答[じもんじとう]}を繰[く]り返[かえ]した。
ctx.en: For days I went back and forth with myself over whether to quit my job.

ctx.s: この小説[しょうせつ]は、主人公[しゅじんこう]の{自問自答[じもんじとう]}を中心[ちゅうしん]に物語[ものがたり]が進[すす]んでいく。
ctx.en: This novel moves forward mainly through the hero's inner questioning.

bad.en: (meant: the two kept questioning and answering each other for an hour in the meeting)

cards.mean: producing everything one needs by oneself
cards.lit: supplying oneself and meeting one's own needs

use.how: 自給自足の生活 / Xを自給自足する: said of a household, village or country producing its own food, energy or goods instead of buying them.

cards.cue: A couple moves to the mountains, grows their own rice and vegetables, keeps chickens and hardly ever goes shopping.

ctx.en: On this island, people used to produce all their own food.

ctx.en: More and more homes generate all their own electricity with solar power.

cards.mean: opinion divided between those for and against
cards.lit: both arguments: approval and disapproval

cards.cue: A famous series ends with a shocking twist: half the fans call it a masterpiece and the other half call it a betrayal.

bad.en: (meant: I have mixed feelings about that plan)

cards.mean: malicious lies and insults that damage someone
cards.lit: slandering and wounding someone with false words

bad.en: (meant: after the match I criticised my own mistakes and reflected on them)

cards.mean: all preparations done and ready to go
cards.lit: preparations made in every one of ten thousand details

use.how: 準備万端だ / 準備万端で臨む / 準備万端整う: said of being fully ready for a particular event, trip or task right now.

bad.en: (meant: on cleaning day I polished every corner of the room thoroughly)
bad.why: It says preparations are complete and you are ready; it is not an adverb for doing a job thoroughly. Say tetteiteki ni migaita.

bad.s: まだ何[なに]もしていないから、そろそろ{準備万端[じゅんびばんたん]}を始[はじ]めよう。
bad.en: (meant: I haven't done anything yet, so let's start getting ready)
bad.why: It means the preparations are already finished, so it cannot be something you start. Say junbi o hajimeyou.

cards.mean: excelling at both studies and sport
cards.lit: both paths: the way of letters and the way of arms, once the ideal of the samurai

near.diff: 才色兼備 praises a woman for both talent and beauty; 文武両道 praises anyone for both studies and sport.

cards.mean: so closely united they act as one body and mind
cards.lit: one heart, the same body: two or more people sharing a single mind and body

一致団結 is a group pulling together for a goal; 一心同体 stresses an inseparable bond, often between just two parties.

cards.cue: A comedy duo has worked together for thirty years; when one is praised or blamed, the other feels it as his own. How do they describe themselves?

ctx.en: We're one and the same, so your happiness is my happiness.

ctx.s: 会社[がいしゃ]と社員[しゃいん]が{一心同体[いっしんどうたい]}となって、危機[きき]を乗[の]り越[こ]えた。

bad.en: (meant: the meat and vegetables in this curry blend together nicely)

cards.mean: concentrating on one task with no distraction at all
cards.lit: one mind, not scattered: the whole mind held on a single thing

story.text: The phrase comes from the Amida Sutra, which teaches that a person who holds the name of Amida Buddha in mind for one to seven days, with a single mind that does not waver, will see Amida and his attendants appear at the hour of death. 一生懸命 is trying hard in general; 一心不乱 says the attention never strays from the one thing being done.

cards.mean: catching a whole gang in one sweep

cards.mean: settling a matter decisively at one stroke
cards.lit: one stroke of the sword cuts the thing clean in two

cards.mean: good and bad deeds bring matching consequences

near.diff: 自業自得 blames a person for trouble they brought on themselves; 因果応報 states the general law that deeds come back in kind, good or bad.

cards.mean: firmly resolving to take something on
cards.lit: a single thought rises up: one moment of resolve that sets a person on a new path

story.text: It is short for the Buddhist phrase ichinen hokki bodaishin, the moment a person's heart turns and they resolve to seek enlightenment. It came to mean making up one's mind, at a turning point, to start some major undertaking.

use.how: Usually 一念発起して〜する: introduces a big new effort someone resolved on after a turning point (studying for a qualification, quitting a habit, starting a business).

near.diff: 心機一転 is a change of mood to make a fresh start; 一念発起 is a firm resolution to take on a specific, demanding goal.

cards.mean: carrying one's original goal through to the end

near.diff: 有言実行 is doing what you announced you would do; 初志貫徹 is sticking with your original goal over a long time despite setbacks.

bad.why: The whole point is keeping the goal you started with; changing it halfway is the opposite.

cards.mean: quietly acting without talking about it first
cards.lit: no words, only action: doing it without saying you will

use.how: 不言実行の人 / 不言実行で〜する / 不言実行タイプ: praises someone who gets things done without announcing or boasting about them.

near.diff: 有言実行 is announcing your goal and then achieving it; 不言実行 is achieving it without having said anything first.

ctx.en: My grandfather lived by the rule of doing rather than saying, and never once boasted.

bad.en: (meant: he declared he would win and then did)

bad.en: (meant: he skipped the meeting without telling anyone)
bad.why: It praises quietly getting worthwhile things done; slipping away from a duty without a word is not that.

cards.mean: improving together through friendly rivalry
cards.lit: cutting and filing bone and ivory, carving and polishing jade and stone

story.text: An ode in the Book of Songs praises a noble man as finely worked as bone and ivory that has been cut and filed, and jade and stone that has been carved and polished. In the Analects, the disciple Zigong quotes these lines to Confucius to describe how a person refines learning and character, and Confucius is pleased. In Japanese it is now used mostly of friends or rivals who spur each other on.

use.how: 切磋琢磨する / 切磋琢磨し合う / 切磋琢磨しながら: said of classmates, teammates or rivals who push each other to improve.

near.diff: 二人三脚 is two people cooperating toward one shared goal; 切磋琢磨 is peers competing and encouraging each other so each improves.

cards.cue: Two young pianists from the same school enter every contest against each other, and each practises harder because of the other. How would you describe their relationship?

ctx.s: 二人[ふたり]はライバルとして{切磋琢磨[せっさたくま]}してきた。

cards.mean: fighting a hard, desperate battle

孤軍奮闘 stresses fighting alone without help; 悪戦苦闘 stresses how hard the fight is.

cards.mean: struggling alone without anyone's support

cards.mean: completely worn out with fatigue
cards.lit: fatigue piled up until one's strength is completely spent

不眠不休 describes the effort of working without sleep or rest; 疲労困憊 is the drained state that results.

cards.r: きょうぞんきょうえい

ctx.en: This book is a side-splitting collection of essays about the author's life abroad.

bad.en: (meant: she gave a quiet smile)
bad.why: It means roaring, helpless laughter, so it cannot describe a quiet smile; the sentence contradicts itself.

bad.s: 試験[しけん]に合格[ごうかく]して、うれしくて{抱腹絶倒[ほうふくぜっとう]}した。
bad.en: (meant: I passed the exam and was overjoyed)
bad.why: It is laughter at something funny, not happiness or delight. For joy say ooyorokobi shita (was overjoyed).

cards.mean: mostly the same, with only minor differences
cards.lit: largely the same, small differences

story.text: The phrase is traced to the last chapter of the Zhuangzi, which lists the paradoxes of the logician Hui Shi about large and small sameness and difference. Japanese uses it for things that are basically the same, with only trivial differences.

use.how: Xは大同小異だ or 大同小異のN: said of plans, products, opinions or results compared side by side, often implying there is little to choose between them.

near.diff: 千差万別 stresses that things differ endlessly; 大同小異 says the opposite, that they are basically alike.

bad.s: 二[ふた]つの案[あん]は{大同小異[だいどうしょうい]}で、まったく違[ちが]う。
bad.en: (meant: the two plans are completely different)

cards.mean: the one and only; nothing else like it
cards.lit: only one, no second

near.diff: 天下一品 ranks quality: the very best of its kind; 唯一無二 says there is nothing else like it at all, whatever its rank.

ctx.en: That director is known for a style that no one can imitate.

cards.mean: the finest of its kind anywhere
cards.lit: the number one article under heaven

cards.mean: an achievement no one has ever reached before
cards.lit: a point that no one before has reached

near.diff: 空前絶後 adds that it will probably never happen again, and can describe any huge event; 前人未到 praises a first-ever achievement.

cards.mean: never seen before and unlikely ever to be seen again
cards.lit: empty before, cut off after: nothing like it before or since

near.diff: 前人未到 praises a first-ever achievement by someone; 空前絶後 describes any extraordinary event or scale, good or bad, as unique in all time.
前代未聞 says nothing like it was ever heard of, often of something shocking; 空前絶後 adds that it will never be matched again.

ctx.s: その映画[えいが]は{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}の大[だい]ヒットになった。

ctx.en: "What was it like during the bubble?" "A boom like nothing before or since."

ctx.s: 今回[こんかい]のセールは{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}の安[やす]さだと、店長[てんちょう]が胸[むね]を張[は]る。
ctx.en: The manager proudly claims this sale's prices are the lowest there have ever been or ever will be.

ctx.s: あれほどの大地震[だいじしん]は過去[かこ]になく、今後[こんご]もないだろう。まさに{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}の災害[さいがい]だった。

ctx.s: 一人[ひとり]の作家[さっか]がこれほど多[おお]くの名作[めいさく]を残[のこ]したのは、{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}と言[い]ってよい。

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]の人気[にんき]は{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}で、コンサートのチケットは数秒[すうびょう]で売[う]り切[き]れた。
ctx.en: His popularity was unparalleled; concert tickets sold out in seconds.

bad.s: この店[みせ]は毎年[まいとし]、{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}の売[う]り上[あ]げを更新[こうしん]している。
bad.en: (meant: this shop breaks its sales record every year)
bad.why: Zetsugo means it will never be matched again, which contradicts a record broken every year. Say kako saikou o koushin shite iru.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]の人気[にんき]は{空前絶後[くうぜんぜつご]}した。
bad.en: (meant: his popularity reached an unprecedented level)
bad.why: It is a noun used with no or da, not a verb, so it never takes suru. Say ninki wa kuuzen zetsugo datta.

cards.r: ひゃっぱつひゃくちゅう
cards.mean: hitting the mark every single time
cards.lit: a hundred shots, a hundred hits

story.text: Yang Youji, an archer of the state of Chu, could hit a willow leaf from a hundred paces: a hundred shots, a hundred hits. In the telling, a bystander warned him to stop while his record was perfect, since one miss from fatigue would undo his fame. The tale was told to persuade the Qin general Bai Qi not to push his long winning streak too far.

use.how: Xは百発百中だ or 百発百中のN: said of shooting, guesses, forecasts or tips that are right every time, e.g. 彼女の勘は百発百中だ.

ctx.en: My brother never misses a shot.

ctx.en: "Mum says it'll rain tomorrow." "Her weather guesses are always spot on."

ctx.s: 彼女[かのじょ]の勘[かん]は{百発百中[ひゃっぱつひゃくちゅう]}で、隠[かく]し事[ごと]はすぐにばれる。

cards.mean: perfect, without a single flaw
cards.lit: complete, with nothing missing or chipped

cards.mean: twisting things to one's own advantage
cards.lit: drawing the water into one's own rice field

cards.mean: secretly staging an incident oneself
cards.lit: writing the play oneself and acting in it oneself

cards.mean: open, fair and impartial
cards.lit: public and bright, upright and great: conduct done in the open, with nothing crooked about it

cards.mean: relying on others instead of one's own effort
cards.lit: another's power and the original vow

story.text: The phrase is a Pure Land Buddhist term. Tariki, 'other power', is the power of Amida Buddha, and hongan, the 'original vow', is his vow to bring to his Pure Land all beings who entrust themselves to him and call his name. Shinran, founder of the Jōdo Shinshū school, taught that salvation comes through this vow, not through one's own power (jiriki). The everyday sense of leaning on other people is a later secular shift, and the Shin schools object to it.
story.source: Pure Land Buddhism (浄土教), Jōdo Shinshū teaching

cards.mean: seasoned by long, hard experience
cards.lit: a hundred battles, forged and polished: tempered like steel by countless fights

cards.cue: A hostage negotiator has handled hundreds of cases and stays calm whatever is thrown at her. How do colleagues describe her with respect?

cards.mean: worldly-wise and crafty from long experience

near.diff: 百戦錬磨 is respect for skill hardened by experience; 海千山千 warns that the experienced person is wily and not to be trusted.

bad.en: (meant: our class teacher is very experienced and truly admirable)

cards.mean: groping in the dark for a solution

story.text: In the Tang dynasty the official Xu Jingzong was known for forgetting the faces of people he met. 試行錯誤 is improving through repeated tries and mistakes; 暗中模索 stresses that there is no guide or clue to start from.

ctx.en: In a scenic spot surrounded by a lake and mountains stands a small inn.

cards.mean: a blend of Japanese and Western styles
cards.lit: Japanese and Western, met halfway: taking the parts of each and combining them

near.diff: 和魂洋才 is keeping a Japanese spirit while adopting Western learning; 和洋折衷 is mixing Japanese and Western styles in things you can see or taste.

bad.en: (meant: this curry is a fusion of Indian and Thai styles)

bad.en: (meant: he found a compromise between two people's opinions at the meeting)
bad.why: It is about mixing Japanese and Western styles in things, not compromising between opinions; for that say setchūan o dasu.

cards.mean: hopelessly out of step with the times
cards.lit: an error about the era: something placed in a time where it does not belong, an anachronism

use.how: 時代錯誤な考え / 時代錯誤のルール / 時代錯誤だ / 時代錯誤も甚だしい: a sharp criticism of an idea, rule or remark that belongs to a past age.

near.diff: 旧態依然 says an organisation or system has failed to change; 時代錯誤 says an idea or practice clashes with present-day values.

ctx.s: 「毎日[まいにち]残業[ざんぎょう]するのが美徳[びとく]だなんて、ちょっと{時代錯誤[じだいさくご]}じゃない？」
ctx.en: "Saying that working overtime every day is a virtue: isn't that a bit out of date?"

ctx.en: That period drama had an anachronistic blunder: a samurai on screen wearing a wristwatch.

bad.s: このパソコンは五年前[ごねんまえ]のもので、少[すこ]し{時代錯誤[じだいさくご]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: this computer is five years old, so it's a bit outdated)

bad.s: 祖母[そぼ]の着物[きもの]姿[すがた]は{時代錯誤[じだいさくご]}で、とても美[うつく]しい。
bad.en: (meant: my grandmother in her kimono looks classic and beautiful)

cards.mean: stuck in the same old ways, unchanged
cards.lit: the old state, just as before: things remaining exactly as they used to be

use.how: Usually 旧態依然とした / 旧態依然たる + noun, or 旧態依然のままだ: criticises an organisation, system or practice that has failed to change or improve.

near.diff: 時代錯誤 attacks an idea as belonging to a past age; 旧態依然 stresses that nothing has changed despite the need to change.

bad.en: (meant: my grandmother is ninety and still as healthy as ever)

bad.en: (meant: this town keeps its beautiful old streetscape)

cards.mean: the old steadily being replaced by the new
cards.lit: the new replaces the old: also the everyday word for the body's metabolism

use.how: A noun: 新陳代謝が活発だ / 新陳代謝を図る / 組織の新陳代謝。 Said of the body's metabolism, and of organisations, industries or towns renewing their members.

near.diff: 心機一転 is one person changing their attitude for a fresh start; 新陳代謝 is an ongoing renewal in a body or a group.
日進月歩 is rapid progress, as in technology; 新陳代謝 is old members or parts steadily giving way to new ones.

cards.cue: A club run by the same veterans for twenty years decides to bring in young members and let older ones step back, so it keeps renewing itself. What does it need?

ctx.en: Exercise speeds up your metabolism.

ctx.s: この商店街[しょうてんがい]では、古[ふる]い店[みせ]が閉[し]まって新[あたら]しい店[みせ]ができる{新陳代謝[しんちんたいしゃ]}が続[つづ]いている。

cards.mean: rules from above changed as soon as they are made
cards.lit: ordered in the morning, changed by evening

story.text: In a memorial to Emperor Wen of the Former Han, the statesman Chao Cuo described the hard life of farmers. Besides toiling through every season and suffering floods and droughts, he wrote, they faced harsh government and taxes demanded at no fixed time: an order given in the morning was changed by evening. The phrase came to stand for authorities whose orders cannot be relied on.

use.how: 朝令暮改だ / 朝令暮改の方針 / 朝令暮改に振り回される: criticises a government, company or school whose policies and instructions keep changing soon after they are issued.

near.diff: 二転三転 is any story, plan or situation shifting again and again; 朝令暮改 is orders and policies from those in charge being reversed soon after issue.
臨機応変 praises adapting flexibly to circumstances; 朝令暮改 criticises instructions that change so often no one can follow them.

ctx.en: "The boss changed his instructions again?" "He really does change his orders as soon as he gives them."

ctx.en: Reviewing a policy isn't bad in itself, but it needs careful explanation so it isn't seen as flip-flopping.

bad.en: (meant: he is a dependable leader who adapts his plans to the situation)

bad.en: (meant: today's weather kept changing between sun and rain)
bad.why: It is about orders and policies from people in charge, not weather; say tenki ga kawariyasui.

cards.mean: a sudden turn that brings things to a resolution
cards.lit: a sudden turn, then straight down: events abruptly change course and drop to a conclusion

use.how: Adverbially before a verb of settling (急転直下、解決した / 急転直下決着する) or 急転直下の展開: said of negotiations, cases or stories that suddenly turn and are settled.

near.diff: 二転三転 is a matter shifting again and again without settling; 急転直下 is one sudden turn after which it is quickly settled.

bad.en: (meant: his grades rose steadily over a year)

cards.mean: a story or situation that keeps shifting
cards.lit: turning twice, turning three times: changing direction again and again

急転直下 is one sudden turn that settles things; 二転三転 is shift after shift with no settled outcome yet.

bad.en: (meant: it was hot last night and I tossed and turned in bed)

bad.en: (meant: since moving, my life has changed completely for the better)
bad.why: It means repeated reversals, not one big change for the better; say seikatsu ga ippen shita.

cards.mean: the rise and fall of fortunes
cards.lit: flourishing and withering, thriving and declining: like plants, prosperity grows and fades

near.diff: 諸行無常 is the Buddhist truth that nothing at all lasts; 栄枯盛衰 is specifically prosperity followed by decline, often in cycles.

cards.mean: nothing in this world lasts forever

story.text: The idea comes from the Zuo Zhuan, which praises the Spring and Autumn Annals for the way their wording 'punishes evil and encourages good'. ctx.s: 不正[ふせい]に加担[かたん]した幹部[かんぶ]たちは、{一蓮托生[いちれんたくしょう]}で責任[せきにん]を問[と]われた。

bad.en: (meant: relying on no one, he resolved to stake everything himself)

cards.mean: waiting impatiently, each day feeling like years
cards.lit: one day feels like a thousand autumns

story.text: In a love song of the Book of Songs, the singer pines for someone gathering herbs: one day without seeing them is like three months, like three autumns, like three years. use.how: Almost always 一日千秋の思いで待つ / 待ちわびる: waiting eagerly for a person, news or day that you long for. Polite in letters.

bad.en: (meant: the boring meeting dragged on and on)
bad.why: It expresses eager longing for something to come, not boredom with something that won't end.

cards.mean: the greatest attempt of one's whole life
cards.lit: once in one's whole life and generation

story.text: Originally a term of the noh and kabuki stage: an actor, usually before retiring, would perform one of his famous roles for the last time as the crowning performance of his career. From this it came to mean the biggest, once-in-a-lifetime undertaking of anyone's life.

use.how: 一世一代の + noun: 大勝負, 決断, プロポーズ, 晴れ舞台. Said of a person's own single, biggest act or occasion.

near.diff: 一発勝負 is any contest settled in one try; 一世一代 is the biggest undertaking of a whole lifetime.

cards.cue: After years of saving and nerves, he kneels in front of everyone at the restaurant and opens the ring box. What kind of proposal is it?

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]は{一世一代[いっせいちだい]}のプロポーズをした。
ctx.en: He made the proposal of his life.

ctx.s: 「これは僕[ぼく]にとって{一世一代[いっせいちだい]}の大勝負[おおしょうぶ]なんだ」
ctx.en: "This is the biggest gamble of my life."

ctx.s: 「{一世一代[いっせいちだい]}の晴[は]れ舞台[ぶたい]だね」と、母[はは]は結婚式[けっこんしき]の朝[あさ]に言[い]った。

ctx.en: Staking everything he had on opening the shop was the decision of my father's life.

bad.en: (meant: I intend to go jogging every day for the rest of my life)
bad.why: It is not 'all one's life' (that is isshō); it marks one single, biggest act or occasion.

bad.s: 今日[きょう]の昼[ひる]ごはんは、{一世一代[いっせいちだい]}のカップラーメンにした。
bad.en: (meant: for lunch today I just had an ordinary cup noodle)
bad.why: It marks the single biggest act or occasion of a whole life, never a trivial everyday choice.

cards.mean: working oneself to the bone for a cause
cards.lit: grinding one's bones to powder and breaking one's body: giving everything, body included, to a task

use.how: 粉骨砕身努力する / 粉骨砕身の覚悟で: a solemn pledge of total devotion to a role, organisation or cause, typical of speeches by new appointees; also said in praise of others.

near.diff: 一生懸命 is everyday 'doing your best' at anything; 粉骨砕身 is a solemn, formal vow of total self-sacrifice for an organisation or cause.

cards.cue: A newly elected mayor closes her acceptance speech by vowing to give body and soul to the town. Which phrase does she use?

ctx.s: 会社[かいしゃ]のために{粉骨砕身[ふんこつさいしん]}努力[どりょく]いたします。
ctx.en: I will devote myself body and soul to the company.

ctx.s: 「町[まち]の発展[はってん]のため、{粉骨砕身[ふんこつさいしん]}働[はたら]く覚悟[かくご]です」と新市長[しんしちょう]は語[かた]った。
ctx.en: "I am prepared to give everything I have for the town's development," the new mayor said.

ctx.s: 新[しん]キャプテンとして、{粉骨砕身[ふんこつさいしん]}の覚悟[かくご]でチームを引[ひ]っ張[ぱ]ります。
ctx.en: As the new captain, I am ready to give my all to lead the team.

ctx.en: After the war, my grandfather worked himself to the bone for his family.

ctx.s: 被災地[ひさいち]の復興[ふっこう]に{粉骨砕身[ふんこつさいしん]}してきた職員[しょくいん]たちが表彰[ひょうしょう]された。
ctx.en: The staff who had devoted themselves to rebuilding the disaster area were honoured.

bad.en: (meant: I threw myself into my homework and finished it in ten minutes)
bad.why: It is a solemn vow of self-sacrifice for a cause or organisation; for a quick everyday task it sounds absurd. Say isshōkenmei.

bad.s: 階段[かいだん]から落[お]ちて、{粉骨砕身[ふんこつさいしん]}の大怪我[おおけが]をした。
bad.en: (meant: I fell down the stairs and broke bones)
bad.why: It is only figurative, for total devotion to work or a cause; it never describes real injuries.

cards.mean: surrounded by opponents, with no allies left
cards.lit: Chu songs on all four sides: hearing your own people's songs sung from the enemy camp all around you

story.text: Xiang Yu, king of Chu, was besieged by the Han army at Gaixia. At night he heard the songs of Chu rising from the enemy camp on every side, and cried out in dismay: had Han already taken all of Chu, that there were so many men of Chu among his enemies? Feeling abandoned by his own people, he sang his farewell song, and soon after he died.

use.how: 四面楚歌だ / 四面楚歌の状態に陥る: said of a person or group whose plan or position is opposed by everyone around them, with no one on their side.

near.diff: 絶体絶命 is any desperate fix with no way out, such as physical danger; 四面楚歌 is being isolated because everyone around is against you.

cards.cue: Your proposal is attacked by your boss, your team and the client, and not a single colleague speaks up for you. How do you describe your position?

ctx.s: 会議[かいぎ]で僕[ぼく]の案[あん]に全員[ぜんいん]が反対[はんたい]して、{四面楚歌[しめんそか]}だった。
ctx.en: Everyone at the meeting opposed my plan; I was completely on my own.

ctx.s: 家族[かぞく]全員[ぜんいん]に留学[りゅうがく]を反対[はんたい]されて、まさに{四面楚歌[しめんそか]}だよ。
ctx.en: My whole family is against me studying abroad. I don't have a single ally.

ctx.s: 値上[ねあ]げを決[き]めた店長[てんちょう]は、客[きゃく]にも店員[てんいん]にも責[せ]められて{四面楚歌[しめんそか]}だ。

ctx.s: 提携先[ていけいさき]にも取引銀行[とりひきぎんこう]にも見放[みはな]され、その老舗[しにせ]メーカーは{四面楚歌[しめんそか]}に追[お]い込[こ]まれた。
ctx.en: Abandoned by its partners and its bank alike, the long-established maker found itself without a single ally.

bad.en: (meant: lost on the mountain in the rain, I was in a hopeless situation)
bad.why: It is about people turning against you, not physical danger; for a hopeless predicament use zettai zetsumei.

cards.mean: a strong start that fizzles out
cards.lit: a dragon's head and a snake's tail: something grand at the front that tapers off into something small

story.text: The expression is recorded in the Blue Cliff Record (Hekiganroku), a Chinese collection of Zen dialogues and commentary much read in Japanese Zen. There it is said of a monk whose answer opens with an impressive show, but who, the master suspects, has nothing behind it: a dragon's head that will end in a snake's tail.

use.how: 竜頭蛇尾に終わる / 竜頭蛇尾の〜: said of plans, projects, speeches, stories or matches that open impressively and then peter out.

near.diff: 三日坊主 is a person who quits a new habit within days; 竜頭蛇尾 judges a whole undertaking or work whose grand start dwindles to a weak finish.

cards.cue: A novel opens with a gripping, brilliant first chapter, but the ending is rushed and flat. How does a reviewer sum it up?

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]のスピーチは出[で]だしこそ立派[りっぱ]だったが、{竜頭蛇尾[りゅうとうだび]}だった。
ctx.en: His speech began splendidly, but it fizzled out.

ctx.s: 張[は]り切[き]って始[はじ]めた大掃除[おおそうじ]も、結局[けっきょく]{竜頭蛇尾[りゅうとうだび]}に終[お]わった。
ctx.en: I started the big clean-up full of energy, but in the end it petered out.

ctx.en: This novel has a brilliant opening, but the ending is sloppy; it feels like it ran out of steam.

cards.mean: living a leisurely life free of worries, as in retirement
cards.lit: calm and unhurried, doing what suits oneself: living entirely at one's own pace

use.how: 悠々自適の生活 / 悠々自適に暮らす: describes a way of life free of work and worry, above all that of retired people living as they please.

near.diff: 自由奔放 is a free-spirited character that ignores convention; 悠々自適 is a calm, comfortable way of life without work or money worries.

cards.cue: After forty years at the bank, your uncle spends his days fishing, reading and gardening, with no boss and no worries. How do you describe his life?

bad.en: (meant: an old train is running along at a leisurely pace)

cards.mean: two sides of the same thing, inseparable
cards.lit: front and back as one body: like the two faces of a single sheet of paper

bad.en: (meant: my best friend and I are inseparable and go everywhere together)

cards.mean: a husband who rules the household
cards.lit: the master of the house as kanpaku, the emperor's chief minister: the husband rules at home like the highest official

ctx.s: 昔[むかし]は{亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}な家庭[かてい]が多[おお]かったと、祖母[そぼ]は言[い]う。
ctx.en: My grandmother says that in the old days many households were ruled by the husband.

ctx.s: {亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}に見[み]える彼[かれ]も、実[じつ]は家[いえ]では妻[つま]に頭[あたま]が上[あ]がらないらしい。
ctx.en: He looks like a husband who rules the roost, but apparently at home he can't stand up to his wife.

ctx.s: 夫[おっと]の{亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}ぶりに、妻[つま]はとうとう我慢[がまん]できなくなった。
ctx.en: The wife finally had enough of her husband lording it over her at home.

ctx.s: ドラマの父親[ちちおや]は典型的[てんけいてき]な{亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}で、帰[かえ]るなり「飯[めし]！」と言[い]う。
ctx.en: The father in the drama is a typical domineering husband who shouts "Dinner!" the moment he gets home.

bad.s: うちの部長[ぶちょう]は{亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}で、会議[かいぎ]では誰[だれ]にも反論[はんろん]させない。
bad.en: (meant: our manager is domineering and lets no one argue in meetings)
bad.why: It describes a husband's role at home toward his wife, not a domineering boss at work; say wanman or dokusaiteki.

bad.s: 姉[あね]は{亭主関白[ていしゅかんぱく]}で、夫[おっと]に家事[かじ]を全部[ぜんぶ]やらせている。
bad.en: (meant: my sister rules her home and makes her husband do all the housework)
bad.why: Teishu means the husband; a wife who rules the household is the opposite, kakā denka.

cards.mean: again and again, over and over
cards.lit: again, three times, again, four times: repeating something many times over

use.how: Adverb before a verb: 再三再四注意した / 再三再四にわたって要請した. Stresses that warnings, requests or explanations were repeated, usually without effect.

near.diff: 再三 alone means 'repeatedly'; 再三再四 is more emphatic, stressing that it happened many, many times.

cards.cue: The landlord sent warning after warning about the noise, yet the tenant kept playing drums at midnight. How does the landlord's final letter describe the warnings?

ctx.s: 先生[せんせい]に{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}注意[ちゅうい]されたのに、彼[かれ]は遅刻[ちこく]をやめなかった。
ctx.en: Even though the teacher warned him again and again, he kept coming late.

ctx.s: 「{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}お願[ねが]いしているのですが、まだお返事[へんじ]をいただけません」
ctx.en: "I have asked you over and over, but I still haven't received a reply."

ctx.s: 市[し]は住民[じゅうみん]に{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}避難[ひなん]を呼[よ]びかけた。
ctx.en: The city repeatedly urged residents to evacuate.

ctx.s: 息子[むすこ]には{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}言[い]い聞[き]かせてきたが、まだ部屋[へや]を片付[かたづ]けない。
ctx.en: I've told my son time and time again, but he still won't tidy his room.

ctx.s: 審判[しんぱん]は{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}にわたって警告[けいこく]したが、その選手[せんしゅ]は反則[はんそく]を繰[く]り返[かえ]した。
ctx.en: The referee warned him again and again, but the player kept committing fouls.

ctx.s: 管理会社[かんりがいしゃ]から{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}督促状[とくそくじょう]が届[とど]いている。
ctx.en: Payment reminders keep arriving from the management company, one after another.

bad.s: 兄[あに]とは{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}しか会[あ]わない。
bad.en: (meant: I only rarely see my older brother)
bad.why: It means many, many times, not a few times; for 'rarely' say metta ni awanai.

bad.s: 毎朝[まいあさ]、{再三再四[さいさんさいし]}おいしいコーヒーを楽[たの]しんでいる。
bad.en: (meant: every morning I enjoy good coffee, again and again)
bad.why: It stresses repeated warnings or requests, usually unheeded; it is not used for pleasant routines. Say maiasa or itsumo.

cards.mean: every single move or gesture someone makes
cards.lit: each lift, each movement: every action of a person's hands and body

use.how: Noun, usually with に or を: 一挙一動に注目する / 一挙一動を見守る. Said of a person whose every action is watched, copied or scrutinised.

near.diff: 一部始終 is the whole course of events from start to finish; 一挙一動 is every small action or gesture of a person.

cards.cue: A famous actor walks into a small café, and every customer quietly watches how he orders, how he sits, how he lifts his cup. What are they watching?

ctx.s: 赤[あか]ちゃんの{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}がかわいくて、目[め]が離[はな]せない。
ctx.en: Everything the baby does is so cute that I can't take my eyes off her.

ctx.s: 新人[しんじん]の頃[ころ]は、先輩[せんぱい]の{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}を真似[まね]していた。
ctx.en: When I was new, I copied my senior colleague's every move.

ctx.s: 有名人[ゆうめいじん]は{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}が注目[ちゅうもく]されるから大変[たいへん]だ。
ctx.en: Celebrities have it hard, because everything they do is watched.

ctx.s: 面接官[めんせつかん]は、応募者[おうぼしゃ]の{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}を細[こま]かく観察[かんさつ]していた。
ctx.en: The interviewer was closely observing the applicant's every gesture.

ctx.s: 「そんなに私[わたし]の{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}を見張[みは]らないでよ」と娘[むすめ]は不満[ふまん]そうに言[い]った。
ctx.en: "Stop watching every move I make," my daughter said irritably.

ctx.s: ベテラン刑事[けいじ]は、容疑者[ようぎしゃ]の{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}を見逃[みのが]さなかった。
ctx.en: The veteran detective didn't miss a single move the suspect made.

bad.s: 難[むずか]しい問題[もんだい]を{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}で解決[かいけつ]した。
bad.en: (meant: I solved the difficult problem in one stroke)
bad.why: It means every little movement a person makes, not 'in one go'; for that say ikkyo ni.

bad.s: 時計[とけい]の針[はり]の{一挙一動[いっきょいちどう]}が気[き]になる。
bad.en: (meant: I keep noticing every movement of the clock's hands)
bad.why: It describes the actions and gestures of a person, not the movement of machines or objects.

cards.mean: rivals thrown together in the same situation
cards.lit: Wu and Yue in the same boat: people of two enemy states sharing a single boat

story.text: In The Art of War, Sunzi says that the people of Wu and the people of Yue hate each other, yet if they were crossing a river in the same boat and a storm struck, they would help each other as the left hand helps the right. He uses it to show how shared danger makes even enemies act as one.

use.how: まさに呉越同舟だ / 呉越同舟の〜: said when rivals or enemies end up in the same place or are forced to work together, such as rival firms in one project.

near.diff: 一蓮托生 is allies sharing one fate for better or worse; 呉越同舟 stresses that the people thrown together are rivals or enemies.

cards.cue: Two rival electronics makers who constantly fight in court team up to develop a shared charging standard. How would a journalist describe the pairing?

ctx.s: ライバル同士[どうし]が同[おな]じチームになるなんて、{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}だね。
ctx.en: Rivals ending up on the same team? Talk about enemies in the same boat.

ctx.s: 犬猿[けんえん]の仲[なか]の二人[ふたり]が隣[となり]の席[せき]に座[すわ]り、まさに{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}だった。
ctx.en: The two, who can't stand each other, were seated side by side: sworn enemies thrown together.

ctx.s: 「あの二人[ふたり]、仲[なか]が悪[わる]いのに同[おな]じ班[はん]なの？」「そう、{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}ってやつだよ」
ctx.en: "Those two don't get along, and they're in the same group?" "Yep, rivals stuck in the same boat."

ctx.s: 激[はげ]しく競[きそ]い合[あ]う二社[にしゃ]が手[て]を組[く]むという、{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}の共同開発[きょうどうかいはつ]が始[はじ]まった。
ctx.en: A joint development has begun in which two fierce competitors have joined hands, rivals in the same boat.

ctx.s: 地区大会[ちくたいかい]では宿敵[しゅくてき]の二人[ふたり]が、代表[だいひょう]チームでは{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}となった。
ctx.en: The two arch-rivals from the regional tournament found themselves teammates on the national squad.

ctx.s: 大雪[おおゆき]で止[と]まった新幹線[しんかんせん]の中[なか]で、ライバル球団[きゅうだん]の監督[かんとく]二人[ふたり]が{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}の一夜[いちや]を過[す]ごした。
ctx.en: On a bullet train stopped by heavy snow, the managers of two rival baseball teams spent the night stuck together.

bad.s: 仲良[なかよ]しの友達[ともだち]と{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}で旅行[りょこう]に行[い]った。
bad.en: (meant: I went on a trip together with my close friends)
bad.why: It is about rivals or enemies thrown together; for close friends travelling together it is simply wrong.

bad.s: 両[りょう]チームは試合中[しあいちゅう]、{呉越同舟[ごえつどうしゅう]}で激[はげ]しくぶつかり合[あ]った。
bad.en: (meant: the two teams clashed fiercely during the match)
bad.why: It means rivals sharing one situation or side, not rivals fighting each other head-on.

cards.mean: enduring long hardship to win revenge or a comeback
cards.lit: lying on firewood and tasting gall: keeping pain close so as never to forget a defeat

story.text: King Fuchai of Wu, whose father had died of wounds from a battle with Yue, slept on rough firewood so that the pain would keep his vow of revenge alive, and he went on to defeat King Goujian of Yue. Goujian in turn kept a bitter gall bladder by him and tasted it to remember his humiliation, and years later he destroyed Wu.
story.source: 『十八史略』、『史記』越王句践世家

use.how: 臥薪嘗胆の日々 / 臥薪嘗胆の末に〜: describes long, hard endurance after a defeat, with a fixed goal of revenge or a comeback.

near.diff: 捲土重来 is the comeback itself, returning in force after defeat; 臥薪嘗胆 is the long, painful endurance that prepares for it.

cards.cue: After a humiliating loss in the final, the team trains in grim silence for three years with one aim: to beat the champions. How are those years described?

ctx.s: 去年[きょねん]負[ま]けた相手[あいて]に勝[か]つため、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}の一年[いちねん]を過[す]ごした。
ctx.en: I spent a year of grim endurance to beat the opponent who defeated me last year.

ctx.s: 受験[じゅけん]に失敗[しっぱい]した兄[あに]は、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}の末[すえ]、翌年[よくねん]第一志望[だいいちしぼう]に合格[ごうかく]した。
ctx.en: After failing his entrance exams, my brother endured a hard year and got into his first-choice school the next time.

ctx.s: 「この悔[くや]しさを忘[わす]れず、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}の思[おも]いで次[つぎ]の大会[たいかい]に臨[のぞ]もう」と主将[しゅしょう]は言[い]った。
ctx.en: "Let's never forget how this feels, and grit our teeth all the way to the next tournament," the captain said.

ctx.s: 倒産[とうさん]から十年[じゅうねん]、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}の日々[ひび]を経[へ]て、彼[かれ]は再[ふたた]び会社[かいしゃ]を立[た]ち上[あ]げた。
ctx.en: Ten years after his bankruptcy, after long days of hardship, he started a company again.

ctx.s: 初戦敗退[しょせんはいたい]から三年[さんねん]、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}してきたチームがついに優勝[ゆうしょう]した。
ctx.en: Three years after going out in the first round, the team that had endured so much finally won the title.

ctx.s: その映画[えいが]は、国[くに]を滅[ほろ]ぼされた王子[おうじ]の{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}を描[えが]いている。
ctx.en: The film depicts the long, bitter endurance of a prince whose kingdom was destroyed.

bad.s: 初[はじ]めての試験[しけん]に向[む]けて、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}で毎日[まいにち]勉強[べんきょう]している。
bad.en: (meant: I'm studying hard every day for my first exam)
bad.why: It needs a past defeat or humiliation to avenge or overcome; plain hard work toward a first goal is isshōkenmei or doryoku.

bad.s: 隣[となり]の工事[こうじ]がうるさいけど、{臥薪嘗胆[がしんしょうたん]}で我慢[がまん]している。
bad.en: (meant: the construction next door is noisy, but I'm putting up with it)
bad.why: It is long endurance aimed at revenge or a comeback, not simply putting up with an annoyance.

cards.mean: the finishing touch that brings a work to life
cards.lit: painting a dragon and dotting in its eyes last

story.text: The painter Zhang Sengyou painted four dragons on a temple wall in Jinling but left out their eyes, saying that if he painted them the dragons would fly away. People laughed and pressed him, so he dotted the eyes of two. At once there was thunder and lightning, the two dragons broke through the wall and flew up into the sky, and only the two without eyes remained.

use.how: Mostly in 画竜点睛を欠く: a work or plan good overall but missing the one key final touch. Also 〜が画竜点睛となる. Read がりょう, not がりゅう.

near.diff: 有終の美 is finishing a long effort well; 画竜点睛 is the small decisive touch that makes a work come alive.

cards.cue: A well-written speech has no closing line, so it falls flat at the end. What do you say it lacks?

ctx.s: このスピーチは内容[ないよう]はいいが、最後[さいご]のまとめがなく{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}を欠[か]いている。
ctx.en: The speech has good content, but with no summing-up at the end it lacks the finishing touch.

ctx.s: 「このポスター、何[なに]か物足[ものた]りないね」「キャッチコピーがないんだよ。{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}を欠[か]いてる」
ctx.en: "This poster feels like it's missing something." "There's no slogan. It lacks the finishing touch."

ctx.s: 計画[けいかく]は立派[りっぱ]だが、予算[よさん]の裏付[うらづ]けがないのは{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}を欠[か]く。
ctx.en: The plan is impressive, but without the budget to back it, the crucial last piece is missing.

ctx.s: 最後[さいご]に散[ち]らした山椒[さんしょう]の葉[は]が、この料理[りょうり]の{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}となった。
ctx.en: The sansho leaves scattered on at the end were the touch that brought the dish to life.

ctx.s: 試合[しあい]を支配[しはい]しながら決勝点[けっしょうてん]が奪[うば]えず、{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}を欠[か]く結果[けっか]に終[お]わった。
ctx.en: They dominated the match but could not score the winner, so the result lacked its finishing touch.

ctx.s: ラストシーンの主人公[しゅじんこう]の一言[ひとこと]が、映画[えいが]全体[ぜんたい]の{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}になっている。
ctx.en: The hero's single line in the last scene is what brings the whole film to life.

bad.s: 宿題[しゅくだい]が全部[ぜんぶ]終[お]わって、{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: all my homework is done, everything is finished)
bad.why: It is not finishing a task; it is the one small final touch that makes a work come alive, usually said as missing.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は細[こま]かい所[ところ]までこだわる{画竜点睛[がりょうてんせい]}な人[ひと]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is a perfectionist who cares about every detail)
bad.why: It names a finishing touch in a work, not a trait of a person, and it cannot be used as a na-adjective.

cards.mean: fooled by a difference that is only on the surface
cards.lit: three in the morning, four in the evening

story.text: A man in the state of Song kept monkeys and, running short of food, told them they would get three nuts in the morning and four in the evening. The monkeys were furious. So he said: then four in the morning and three in the evening. The monkeys were delighted, though the total was the same.
story.source: 『列子』黄帝篇（『荘子』斉物論にも）

use.how: 〜は朝三暮四だ / 朝三暮四のごまかし: said of a change that looks better but is the same in total, or of being taken in by one.

near.diff: 朝令暮改 is orders that keep changing; 朝三暮四 is a change that only looks like a gain while the total stays the same.

cards.cue: Your monthly loan payment drops, but you now pay for twice as long, so the total is the same. Why are you unimpressed?

ctx.s: 月々[つきづき]の支払[しはら]いが減[へ]っても回数[かいすう]が増[ふ]えるだけなら、{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}だ。
ctx.en: If the monthly payments go down but there are just more of them, it's the same deal dressed up.

ctx.s: 「休[やす]みが一日[いちにち]増[ふ]えたぞ！」「でも別[べつ]の日[ひ]が出勤[しゅっきん]になるんでしょ？{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}だよ」
ctx.en: "We got an extra day off!" "But another day becomes a workday, right? Nothing has really changed."

ctx.s: 基本給[きほんきゅう]を上[あ]げてボーナスを減[へ]らすのでは、社員[しゃいん]にとって{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}にすぎない。
ctx.en: Raising base pay while cutting the bonus is, for employees, a gain in appearance only.

ctx.s: 値下[ねさ]げをうたいながら送料[そうりょう]を上[あ]げるのは、{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}のごまかしだ。
ctx.en: Advertising a price cut while raising the shipping fee is a trick: it looks cheaper, but the total is the same.

ctx.s: ポイント還元[かんげん]に喜[よろこ]んだが、実質[じっしつ]は同[おな]じ値段[ねだん]で、{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}の猿[さる]になった気分[きぶん]だ。
ctx.en: I was pleased about the points back, but the real price is the same; I feel like the monkeys in the fable.

ctx.s: 目先[めさき]の数字[すうじ]に飛[と]びつく消費者[しょうひしゃ]を、評論家[ひょうろんか]は{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}だと皮肉[ひにく]った。
ctx.en: The critic mocked consumers who jump at the number in front of them without seeing the total.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}で、意見[いけん]がすぐに変[か]わる。
bad.en: (meant: he is fickle and changes his opinion from morning to evening)
bad.why: Constant changing is chourei bokai; this idiom is about a change that is the same in total.

bad.s: 父[ちち]は毎日[まいにち]{朝三暮四[ちょうさんぼし]}働[はたら]いている。
bad.en: (meant: my father works from morning till night every day)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with working hours; it is about being fooled by a surface difference.

cards.mean: advertising something better than what is sold
cards.lit: hanging up a sheep's head and selling dog meat

use.how: 〜は羊頭狗肉だ / 羊頭狗肉の商売: criticises goods, services or offers whose advertising or label promises far more than is delivered.

near.diff: 看板倒れ is anything that fails to live up to its name or reputation; 羊頭狗肉 stresses a misleading sign or advert used to sell.

cards.cue: A menu photo shows a thick steak, but the dish that arrives is thin slices of cheap meat. How do you criticise the shop?

ctx.s: 写真[しゃしん]と全然[ぜんぜん]違[ちが]う料理[りょうり]が出[で]てきた。まさに{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}だ。
ctx.en: A dish completely different from the photo came out. Talk about false advertising.

ctx.s: 「天然[てんねん]温泉[おんせん]」とうたいながら水道水[すいどうすい]を沸[わ]かしていたとは、{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}もはなはだしい。
ctx.en: Calling it a natural hot spring while heating tap water is outrageous false advertising.

ctx.s: 派手[はで]な広告[こうこく]の割[わり]に中身[なかみ]が薄[うす]いこの本[ほん]は、{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}と言[い]われても仕方[しかた]がない。
ctx.en: For all its flashy advertising, this book has little in it; no wonder people call it a sham.

ctx.s: 「うちは{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}の商売[しょうばい]はしません」と店主[てんしゅ]は胸[むね]を張[は]った。
ctx.en: "We don't sell anything that isn't what the sign says," the shopkeeper said proudly.

ctx.s: 「高級[こうきゅう]ホテル並[な]み」という宿[やど]の宣伝[せんでん]は、{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}の典型[てんけい]だった。
ctx.en: The inn's ad, "as good as a luxury hotel", was a textbook case of false advertising.

ctx.s: 求人[きゅうじん]広告[こうこく]と実際[じっさい]の仕事[しごと]があまりに違[ちが]い、{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}だと感[かん]じた。
ctx.en: The actual job was so different from the job ad that I felt I had been sold a fake.

bad.s: この店[みせ]は安[やす]いのにとてもおいしい。{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}だね。
bad.en: (meant: surprisingly good for the price)
bad.why: It is the opposite: the product is worse than what was advertised, and it is always a criticism.

bad.s: その店[みせ]は{羊頭狗肉[ようとうくにく]}して客[きゃく]を集[あつ]めた。
bad.en: (meant: the shop drew customers with misleading ads)
bad.why: It is a noun used with da or no, not a verb with suru; say youtou kuniku no senden de (with misleading ads).

cards.mean: onlookers see a situation more clearly than those in it
cards.lit: watching from the side, you see eight moves ahead

story.text: The phrase comes from the game of Go. Someone watching a game from the side, free of the players' tension, is said to read the board eight moves further ahead than the players themselves. From this it came to mean that an outsider judges a situation better than those caught up in it.

use.how: Often 岡目八目で〜がよく見える, or 岡目八目とはよく言ったものだ. Said of an outsider's clearer view; also written 傍目八目.

cards.cue: You can always tell what your friend should do about her relationship, yet you are lost with your own. What saying explains this?

ctx.s: 他人[たにん]の恋愛[れんあい]はよくわかるのに自分[じぶん]のことはさっぱりだ。{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}とはよく言[い]ったものだ。
ctx.en: I understand other people's love lives but not my own. It's true the onlooker sees more.

ctx.s: 「外[そと]から見[み]ている君[きみ]のほうが冷静[れいせい]だね」「{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}ってやつだよ」
ctx.en: "You see it more calmly from the outside." "That's the bystander's advantage."

ctx.s: 将棋[しょうぎ]を横[よこ]で見[み]ていると、{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}で次[つぎ]の一手[いって]がよく見[み]える。
ctx.en: Watching a shogi game from the side, you can see the next move clearly, as onlookers do.

ctx.en: I tend to miss mistakes in my own writing, but in someone else's I spot them at once.

ctx.s: 社外[しゃがい]の人[ひと]に意見[いけん]を聞[き]くと、{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}で思[おも]わぬ問題点[もんだいてん]が見[み]つかる。
ctx.en: Ask someone outside the company and, seeing it from outside, they find problems you never expected.

ctx.s: コンサルタントの強[つよ]みは、{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}の立場[たちば]から助言[じょげん]できることだ。
ctx.en: A consultant's strength is being able to advise from the clearer view of an outsider.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}で、八手[はって]先[さき]まで読[よ]める天才[てんさい]棋士[きし]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is a genius player who reads eight moves ahead)
bad.why: It is about onlookers seeing more than those involved, not about a player's own skill.

bad.s: 人[ひと]の家[いえ]のことに{岡目八目[おかめはちもく]}するのはやめなさい。
bad.en: (meant: stop meddling in other families' affairs)
bad.why: It does not mean nosiness or interfering, and it is not used as a verb with suru.

cards.mean: coming back in force after a defeat
cards.lit: rolling up the dust and coming again

story.text: The Tang poet Du Mu, visiting the Wujiang pavilion where the defeated general Xiang Yu took his own life rather than cross back to his homeland, wrote that victory and defeat cannot be foreseen and that a true man bears his shame; the young men east of the river were many and able, and had he gone back to them, who knows whether he might have rolled up the dust and returned.

use.how: 捲土重来を期す / 誓う / 果たす / 図る, or 捲土重来する: said of a person or team that lost and aims to, or does, come back strongly. Also read けんどじゅうらい.

near.diff: 起死回生 is turning a hopeless situation around in one move; 捲土重来 is regrouping after a defeat and returning later.

cards.cue: A team lost the final; the captain tells reporters they will train all year and return to win. What does the team vow?

ctx.en: The team that lost the final vowed to come back strong next year.

ctx.en: "This year was a letdown, but let's train with our sights set on coming back."

ctx.s: 敗戦[はいせん]の翌朝[よくあさ]、主将[しゅしょう]は「必[かなら]ず{捲土重来[けんどちょうらい]}する」とノートに書[か]いた。
ctx.en: The morning after the defeat, the captain wrote in a notebook: "We will come back."

bad.en: (meant: they won on their very first appearance)
bad.why: It needs an earlier defeat to come back from; a first-time win is not a comeback.

bad.en: (meant: it was windy and dusty)
bad.why: The dust is only an image of an army returning; it is never used about actual weather.

cards.mean: a fighter worth a thousand others

bad.en: (meant: this shop's ramen is unbeatably tasty)

bad.s: 彼女[かのじょ]は千人[せんにん]の観客[かんきゃく]の前[まえ]で、一人[ひとり]で{一騎当千[いっきとうせん]}した。
bad.en: (meant: she performed solo in front of a thousand people)
bad.why: The thousand are rivals one person can match, not an audience, and it is not used as a verb.

cards.mean: in twos and threes, a few at a time
cards.lit: by threes, by fives: people moving in small loose groups

cards.mean: the beauties of nature as celebrated in art
cards.lit: flowers, birds, wind and moon

use.how: 花鳥風月を愛でる / 詠む / 描く / 友とする: nature's gentle beauty as a subject of poetry, painting and refined taste.

near.diff: 風光明媚 praises a particular place's scenery; 花鳥風月 is nature's beauty in general as something to appreciate and portray.

cards.mean: so stunned one is left blank and helpless
cards.lit: dazed and having lost oneself

use.how: 茫然自失となる / する / のまま / の状態: someone left blank and unable to act by a severe shock, loss or disaster. Also written 呆然自失.

near.diff: 意気消沈 is losing heart and being dejected; 茫然自失 is being so shocked one cannot think or act at all.

cards.mean: freely and boldly in every direction
